Valid manual spacing is now preserved exactly when automatic spacing is enabled. Per-link turns and reference gaps use paired sliders with independent resets; automatic references to a self-closed link prefer mirrored turns and equal, close gaps.

- Turns sit together below the separator, cover −180…180° and use one-degree steps. Left/Right, other navigation keys and exact numeric companions work in EN/RU.
- Each of the six geometry values resets independently. Reference gaps use 0…1 sliders while retaining inherited values and precise numeric/spinner editing.
- The solver separates actual collision satisfaction from its turn penalty, preserves every reported valid manual example, and jointly searches mirrored reference ends before the general fallback. The default example now gives −13°/+13° and equal 0.16 gaps, with zero painted collisions and unchanged closed halves.
- Automatic spacing remains experimental and off by default. Search respects the original bounds; existing explicit URL settings, canonicalization, gallery/rain geometry and editor exports are retained.

Reproduce the reported failure with `/network/?code=1111&rotation=-90&turns=0+5%2C-15+15&gaps=0.08+%7E+0%2C0.18+0.18+0`, then enable automatic spacing. Previously it erased the ±15° turns. It now leaves the drawing, Apply result and shared URL rendering identical. The new `issue-29.test.js`, `network-29.test.jsx` and `test:network:issue29` browser suite guard this behavior and the control changes.

Validation: **749 unit/DOM tests pass**, alongside lint, formatting, file-size, secrets, dependency audit, the production build and all six historical URL schemas. title: Pair link sliders and improve automatic spacing

body:
Fixes #27.

Equal reference gaps on a self-closed link now have exactly equal painted extents. The arrow correction uses each closed endpoint's tangent, removing the sudden jump between `0.07` and `0.08`, while retaining issue 25's common painted boundary for a lens referencing another link.

Automatic spacing preserves turns, reference gaps and middle cuts on fully or partially self-closed halves and optimizes open references. Shared URLs omit default turn rows and trailing inherited gap columns, accept every historical URL schema, and replace the address with the compact equivalent on arrival. A shared numeric component preserves intermediate text and inherited values, including native spinner clicks on empty inherited fields; all slider and number renderers support consistent decimal stepping and keyboard navigation.

### Reproduction and verification

Open `/network/?code=1111&rotation=-90&turns=0+0%2C-15+15&gaps=0.08+0.08+%7E+%7E%2C0.18+0.18+%7E+%7E`. Before the fix, source/target painted closed gaps measured **4.15 / 5.45** SVG units; after, **4.15 / 4.15**. Changing only the target from `0.07` to `0.08` now moves it by the expected **0.60**, rather than **1.90** units. The exact manual arrangement is a regression fixture.

- Geometry, full/partial closed-half solver, historical-schema, URL history and numeric editing regressions are included. Failed-before logs, raw numerical measurements and independent rasterized SVG checks are archived.
- `npm run check`, **737 unit tests** and production build pass. `npm run test:network:issue27` runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit alongside all existing browser suites in CI, with screenshots and JSON artifacts. Playwright MCP verifies actual native spinner Up/Down clicks, including inherited values.
- The [case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/cdf0cd1c23ca741354fa076975984cb960176519/docs/case-studies/issue-27/README.md) inventories every requirement, reconstructs the timeline, audits all six historical URL schemas, explains the root causes and alternatives, and includes source data, prior-session logs and [validation evidence](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/cdf0cd1c23ca741354fa076975984cb960176519/docs/case-studies/issue-27/VALIDATION.md).

The solver remains an opt-in overlap heuristic: it preserves the closed link but can choose different open-link gaps/turns from the symmetric manual fixture. Its preview, applied result and shared reload are identical. No external dependency defect was identified in this issue.

Each link now has a responsive card containing all nine existing inputs, with visible gap overrides.

The shared geometry serves the preview, solver, SVG and raster exports. Gallery/rain defaults and existing link actions are preserved. Optional solver diagnostics default off. The bounded search remains heuristic: unattainable clearance within the configured bounds retains its residual score.

Fixes #23.
Fixes #21.

Loading thousands of gallery cards kept a backdrop filter on every card, adding avoidable rendering pressure behind the fixed header. Offscreen cards, repositories and posts now disable their filters through one shared viewport observer; visible panels retain their selected skin. The redundant gallery Share icon is removed, leaving the full-card editor link.

The editor now starts with bend **0**, keeps full and partial self-loops balanced, and offers independent signed loop shaping. Displaced endpoint and middle markers follow arc length and the local tangent. Four optional gaps per link inherit global settings when blank, survive URL sharing/export and saved looks, and participate in the experimental overlap solver. Applying the solver preserves its preview exactly. Legacy gallery, rain and theory geometry remains covered by stored hashes.

The [case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-23-729a1009db7c/docs/case-studies/issue-23/README.md) maps every requirement to its cause, implementation and evidence, including the complete audit of #21, archived reports/logs, research, alternatives and default-off diagnostics. The supplied Safari screenshots document the intermittent blink. Native display captures now verify bounded filter counts and visible blur in Chromium/Firefox on Linux and WebKit on macOS at the full reported load. The exact original Safari GPU failure remains unisolated; optional diagnostics are available for recurrence. A separately reproduced Firefox screenshot defect is reported upstream with a minimal example and workaround: [microsoft/playwright#43646](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43646).

### Reproduction and regression checks

On the original code, open `/network/?code=00000000` to see bent free links, or `/network/?code=11&startOffset=12&endOffset=12` to see displaced markers leave the loop. The old gallery also exposes two links per card and retains 4,131 filters after loading 4,131 cards. Failing geometry and DOM tests and production screenshots were captured before the fix.

- Geometry, curve, solver and DOM regressions cover neutral defaults, signed ranges, native curve placement, individual/inherited gaps, URL round-trips, exact applied previews, list-observer cleanup and a dense 24-link solver scaling regression.
- All four network browser suites run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including real image downloads, source colors, supplied #21 URLs, history, mobile editing and actual composited header blur.
- All three engines pass the exact **4,131-card** load, repeated scrolling and actual display-pixel blur checks in all three skins, with **55–176 active card filters** and zero page errors. A separate audit passes all ten HTML entries across skins, themes, languages and desktop/mobile widths (**240 combinations**).
- **710 unit tests**, lint/format/line limits/secrets, dependency audit, production build and **120 CV PDFs** pass locally; detailed results are in [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-23-729a1009db7c/docs/case-studies/issue-23/VALIDATION.md).

Final head CI is green: [run 40276708061](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40276708061) at `cf1e6ec`, including all browser suites, 710 unit tests, builds and 120 PDFs. The complete source-validation evidence from [run 40275956453](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40275956453) at `0bc96b4` is archived in the case study; the final commit adds only that evidence. `main` is already included, and the working tree is clean.

body:
Fixes #19

Slider changes previously wrote to browser history on every input; Safari's quota exception could remove the editor. History now updates after release and 400 ms of quiet, with bounded retries and exception handling. Preview and share links update immediately. Other history-writing paths receive the same exception protection.

- Fixed self-reference leaving/entering angles, curvature and bend. Hide controls that cannot affect the current network.
- Added independent reference gaps and symmetric start/end/middle marker sizes, angles, tangent/sideways offsets and rotations. Optional cuts on either side of the middle support open rings; the default line stays continuous.
- Applied the requested editor defaults with rotation still zero, while preserving gallery/rain geometry and the gallery preset.
- Added square, hexagonal, dice, playing-card, sunflower and deterministic D3 force placement. Automatic placement uses a circle for 1–4 links. Removed the nine-link limit throughout notations, editing, colours, turns, URLs and exports; large indices/counts remain exact.
- Fixed Safari image clipboard activation by passing a PNG promise to `ClipboardItem` during the click. Native sharing prepares images in advance and retains synchronous link sharing while preparation is pending. Unsupported clipboard capabilities expose download/selectable-link alternatives.
- Corrected large-number fields overflowing their mobile panel and coalesced native-share image rendering during rapid edits.

## Reproduction and tests

The retained [reproduction experiment](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/experiments/issue-19-reproduce.mjs) injects a bounded history quota and records the original blank screen. Failing tests were recorded before each correction; the [case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/README.md) maps every issue requirement to implementation and evidence, including source data, primary-source research, alternatives and default-off diagnostics.

- Unit coverage includes all 4,181 networks with 1–3 links, self-reference controls, marker symmetry, exact cubic cuts, interaction timing, clipboard/share activation, eight placement modes at eleven sizes, and all notation round trips at 10/37/100 links.
- Browser regressions cover 120-event drags, repeated releases, injected history failure/recovery, both complete issue URLs, actual PNG clipboard writes, image downloads, seven distinct layouts, shared-URL reloads and a 100-link touch editor. Existing gallery/editor/export regressions run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI.
- Local checks: ESLint, Prettier, file limits, secret scanning, all 682 unit tests, production build, all 120 CV PDFs and a dependency audit with zero vulnerabilities. Browser engines run sequentially locally; CI preserves screenshots and result JSON for each engine.

Final validation: [CI run 40131510761](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40131510761) passes on the published head `49a22927e75bb29e1806a69c8f2c22ca25311853`: lint, repository checks, all three browser engines, 682 unit tests, production build, all 120 CV PDFs and the Pages artifact. Deployment is intentionally skipped for pull requests. The passing implementation run’s raw logs and browser artifacts are archived in the case study.

Touch tests use browser emulation; operating-system share sheets use gesture-sensitive component tests. The case study records these verification limits. Linux WebKit r2370 has a confirmed upstream backdrop-filter regression ([Playwright #43426](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43426), [WebKit 327850](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327850)); bounded probes reproduce it and verify the documented stable Playwright 1.63.0 pin with the unchanged glass gallery. Full browser suites remain enabled for all three engines; CI runs them on separate runners.

Clicking a gallery card now opens `/network/?code=…` with that exact network. The page edits its notations and individual links, configures its SVG, and downloads or shares the resulting picture. The small share icon appears on hover or keyboard focus and opens the sharing section.

Fixes #17

- Edit theory notation (L → L² or R → R²), pairs, the N-ary number, exact decimal index and links notation. Supports every gallery configuration and networks of 1–9 links, with add/remove, reference editing, previous/next, random and canonical renaming.
- Configure endpoint angles and per-link turns; start/end/middle markers and sizes; curves, loops, spacing, margins and rotation; colours, line styles, opacity and glow; transparent/solid/gradient backgrounds; optional cards and border styles. Includes plain black without a card, presets, captions, image sizes and saved styles.
- Download SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP and `.lino`; copy the link, image or SVG; use native sharing where supported or ten social/email share links. The address preserves the complete picture, theory notation and explicit page language.
- Opt into experimental overlap reduction by adjusting endpoint angles; inspect the score, apply the turns or clear them.

Recovered the interrupted session requested in the PR comment. Reproduced and fixed its unfinished sticky-preview layout, partial notation parsing, inconsistent collision scoring/clamped applied turns, receiver-dependent theory captions and lost language parameters. Each correctness fix has a regression test; the layout has before/after screenshots and a browser visibility assertion.

Verification:

[CI passed on final commit `71d2a9b`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40115390362).

- All 565 unit/data/workflow tests; lint, formatting, line limits, secret scan, production build and dependency audit (0 vulnerabilities).
- Chromium browser checks are now part of CI: gallery navigation, editable notations/invalid input, styling, solver application, URL round trips in a fresh browser, actual downloaded file contents/dimensions/transparency, language reload and 360–1920 px layouts in EN/RU. The browser suite also passed in Firefox.
- All 120 CV PDFs passed the existing page-count, text-layer and reading-order checks.
- Bounded solver experiment: 507 of 720 three-link classes improved, 213 unchanged, none worse. Default gallery/rain SVGs match `main` byte for byte across 4,693 configurations.

To reproduce the original layout bug, open `/network/?code=221331` on desktop and scroll to Style: previously the preview was entirely above the viewport. It now stays beside the controls. Run `npm run build && npm run test:network:browser`; parser/solver/URL regressions are in `src/links/network.test.js` and `src/pages/network.test.jsx`.

| --- | --- |
| ![Preview out of view](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-17-c029b2b48293/docs/case-studies/issue-17/screenshots/before-style-preview.png?raw=true) | ![Sticky preview beside styles](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-17-c029b2b48293/docs/case-studies/issue-17/screenshots/after-style-preview.png?raw=true) |

![Network editor](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-17-c029b2b48293/docs/case-studies/issue-17/screenshots/network-desktop.png?raw=true)

| Plain black, no card | Experimental overlap reduction |
| --- | --- |
| ![Plain black](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-17-c029b2b48293/docs/case-studies/issue-17/screenshots/plain-black.png?raw=true) | ![Reduced overlaps](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-17-c029b2b48293/docs/case-studies/issue-17/screenshots/collisions-after.png?raw=true) |

[Requirement-by-requirement evidence, mobile/light screenshots and reproducible experiments](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-17-c029b2b48293/docs/case-studies/issue-17/README.md).

The overlap solver is a heuristic and remains opt-in. Static social link previews are shared across networks; attach the downloaded/copied image or use native file sharing for the actual picture. Clipboard/native sharing depend on browser support. An optional WebKit run could not finish within the container's 2.92 GiB memory limit (browser lost on the gallery); no passing WebKit run is claimed.

body:
Fixes #15

Each item of the issue is listed below with its solution and the test that checks it. The full analysis is in the case study [`docs/case-studies/issue-15/README.md`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/README.md). It covers every requirement with where it is done and what verifies it, the root causes, the measurements, a comparison with konard/immortality, libraries and online research, and the remaining limits.

## The new defaults, and every setting actually applied

- **Defaults.** The 21 values of the JSON in the issue are the new defaults. `src/settings/settings.test.js` holds that JSON exactly as given and checks that the defaults match it.
- **"Double check that all settings are actually applied."** `src/settings/applied.test.js` goes through all 251 settings and fails for any setting that is not used. A setting counts as used when:
  - a stylesheet uses its CSS variable or attribute;
  - a background layer reads it (recorded through a `Proxy`);
  - a component reads its key.

  A second test checks that every choice of every select has a CSS rule or a script that reads it.

## Space around every rain symbol

- **The setting.** `rain.padding`: free space on every side of a symbol, 0–16 px.
- **Found on the way.** The rain glow was half as large on Retina screens: `shadowBlur` counts canvas pixels, not CSS pixels. It is now scaled by `devicePixelRatio`.
- **Tests.** `src/components/visuals.test.jsx`.

## The Skin block jumped and was misaligned

- **Root cause.** The settings page laid out its sections with CSS multi-column. The browser balances columns by height, and the skin sections differ in height. Choosing liquid instead of glass therefore moved Rain to the other column, and every section after it, Skin included, moved too. In WebKit every section fell into one column with negative tops (−365 and −579 px).
- **How to reproduce.** Run `npm run build && npx vite preview --port 4173`, then `ENGINE=chromium|firefox|webkit node experiments/settings-layout.mjs`. It prints the column of each section for each skin.
  - Before the fix: "sections that change their column between glass and liquid: rain".
  - After the fix: "none", with equal column tops in all three browsers.
  - The logs are in `docs/case-studies/issue-15/data/layout-*.log`.
- **Fix.** Two fixed columns. Every row is one label | control | value | reset grid. In a section with tabs, the settings shared by all tabs come before the tabs.
- **Tests.** `src/pages/settings.test.jsx`.

| Reported | Before, glass | Before, liquid (Rain moved) | After, liquid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![reported](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/issue-reported-4.png?raw=true) | ![before glass](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/settings-before-chromium-glass.png?raw=true) | ![before liquid](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/settings-before-chromium-liquid.png?raw=true) | ![after liquid](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/settings-after-chromium-liquid.png?raw=true) |

| Before, WebKit | After, WebKit |
| --- | --- |
| ![before webkit](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/settings-before-webkit.png?raw=true) | ![after webkit](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/settings-after-webkit.png?raw=true) |

## Polish: the glass skin

- **Blue panels.** The saturation was stored as a plain number, so `saturate(100)` meant ×100 and painted the panels blue. Values above 2 are now divided by 100.
- **Panels without blur.** Page cards, Habr cards, the language cloud and the theory panels had no blur. One rule now gives every panel the blur and radius.
- **New settings, for the questionable choices.** The colour behind panels, borders and lines, the shadow, and the light on the upper edge.
- **Tests.** `src/skins.test.jsx`.

| Dark | Light |
| --- | --- |
| ![glass dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/glass-options-dark.png?raw=true) | ![glass light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/glass-options-light.png?raw=true) |

## Background: levels and detailed settings for every layer

- **Universe.** Strength, speed, gas, hue, four colours, zoom, its own stars (amount, size, colour, brightness, twinkling), vignette, frames per second and resolution.
- **Up to four star layers on top of each other.** Each layer has:
  - 12 shapes: dot, soft, ring, square, diamond, cross, ×, 4-, 5- and 6-pointed stars, sparkle, flare;
  - size and size variety;
  - colour and colour variety, brightness;
  - glow and glow colour;
  - twinkling speed and depth, rotation and spin;
  - motion: still, drift, warp towards you or orbit, with a direction and speed;
  - streaks and blending.
- **Beams: the "effects that go vertically and horizontally".** Light runs along the grid lines, horizontally, vertically or both. Settings: number, speed, length, width, style, colour, glow and pause.
- **Grid.** Styles: lines, dashes, crosses and dots. Also marks, line width, colour, tint and fading.
- **Cost.** The star and beam code is loaded only when a layer is switched on.
- **Tests.** `src/visuals/layers.test.jsx`.

## Futuristic frames: each corner on its own, with preview tiles

- **Each corner** has its own shape and its own line, and one size applies to all corners.
  - 7 shapes: square, cut, tall cut, wide cut, round, scoop, notch.
  - 5 lines: none (a missing border, as before), gap, line, accent, bracket.
- **Tiles.** Every choice is a tile that previews the real corner in the current colours. A button makes every corner like the chosen one.
- **How it is drawn.** `src/skins.frames.js` generates `src/skins.frames.css` (`npm run build:frames`) from `clip-path` polygons and gradient lines. CSS `corner-shape` is not Baseline yet (Chrome and Edge 139+ only, [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/corner-shape)), so polygons are used.
- **Tests.** `src/skins.frames.test.jsx` checks that the stylesheet is up to date, plus the geometry and the tiles.

| Tiles, dark | Tiles, light | A custom frame | Zoomed corners |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![tiles dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/frames-corner-tiles-dark.png?raw=true) | ![tiles light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/frames-corner-tiles-light.png?raw=true) | ![home](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/frames-custom-home.png?raw=true) | ![zoom](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/frames-custom-zoom.png?raw=true) |

## Sound design

- **31 synthesized sounds.** 26 come from konard/immortality (the Unlicense) and 5 are new: raindrop, link, glass, warp, byte. There are no audio files.
- **10 interactions.** Each has up to four sounds with a level for each, played at random, in turn or together.
- **The mix.** Volume, tone, room echo and room size, pitch variation, stereo towards the pointer and its width, and the shortest gap between two sounds.
- **Controls.** A ▶ for every sound and a sound switch in the top bar. Sound is off by default, and its code is loaded only when it is switched on.
- **Root cause of a click in mica.** A `GainNode` starts at 1 until its first event, so one sample of full-scale noise got through, and mica sounded 15 times too loud.
  - Found with `experiments/sound-render.mjs` and `experiments/sound-isolate.mjs`.
  - Fixed with `amp.gain.value = 0`.
- **Tests.** `src/sound/sound.test.jsx` and `src/components/Sound.test.jsx`. `experiments/sound-e2e.mjs` checks it in a real browser.

| Settings, dark | Light | Phone | Top bar, sound on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![sound dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/sound-settings-dark.png?raw=true) | ![sound light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/sound-settings-light.png?raw=true) | ![sound 360](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/sound-settings-360-dark.png?raw=true) | ![top bar](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/sound-topbar-on.png?raw=true) |

## Presets, saved looks and links

- **9 built-in presets**, each with a miniature drawn from its settings: Default, Calm, Matrix, Deep space, Warp, Neon HUD, Liquid, Blueprint, and Light and fast.
- **Saved looks.** Save, apply, update, rename and delete. Copy as JSON and load in another browser. They stay in sync between tabs.
- **A random look.** It is never heavier than the defaults: no more things drawn, frames per second or resolution.
- **A `#settings=` link.** It carries a look and keeps the look it replaced as "Before the link".
- **What a look never changes.** The motion, volume or notation.
- **Cost.** The preset code is loaded only on the settings page or with such a link.
- **Tests.** `src/settings/presets.test.js` and `src/pages/presets.test.jsx`. `experiments/presets-e2e.mjs` checks it in a real browser.

| Presets | Matrix applied | Saved looks | Phone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![presets](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/presets-dark.png?raw=true) | ![matrix](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/presets-matrix.png?raw=true) | ![saved](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/presets-saved.png?raw=true) | ![phone](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/presets-360-dark.png?raw=true) |

## Fast on mobile

`experiments/perf-mobile.mjs` measures a phone: 412×915, a CPU slowed four times, slow 4G, medians of 3 runs. The results are in `data/perf-mobile-{main,branch}.json`.

| Page | FCP, ms | Long tasks, ms | Background frames/s | kB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | 2844 → 3056 | 5405 → 3359 | 6 → 13 | 204 → 217 |
| `/settings/` | 1788 → 2052 | 5293 → 2817 | 6 → 16 | 126 → 128 |
| `/art/` | 2204 → 2416 | 5581 → 3005 | 6 → 19 | 168 → 161 |
| `/blog/` | 2108 → 2064 | 5527 → 3830 | 7 → 15 | 142 → 135 |
| `/cv/` | 1784 → 1864 | 5477 → 2836 | 6 → 21 | 135 → 150 |

- **A governor** (`src/visuals/governor.js`) watches the frame gaps. While the page cannot keep up, it lowers the resolution and then the frame rate of the universe, and the frame rate of stars and beams. The universe is the costly layer: switching it off alone gives 25 frames/s.
- **Smaller shared code.** The code shared by all pages no longer carries the career data. The Layout chunk went from 111.5 to 91.2 kB gzip.
- **Stated plainly.** Long tasks are about 45% shorter and the background runs 2–3× more frames per second. FCP is not better: it is 80–260 ms later on four pages and 44 ms earlier on `/blog/`. The pages are rendered in the browser, and pre-rendering them is a change to the build of every page (see the limits in the case study).
- **Tests.** `src/visuals/governor.test.js`.

## Every screen

`experiments/responsive.mjs` checks 9 pages × 4 widths (360, 768, 1280, 1920) × 2 themes. For each case it checks:

- nothing scrolls sideways;
- no element sticks out of the screen;
- the current page is visible in the top bar, with at least three page links.

**main fails 8 of the 72 cases** (`data/responsive-main.log`): at 360 px, two page links and a hidden current page; at 768 px, `/blog/` hides the current page. **This branch passes 72 of 72.**

- **The fixes.**
  - On phones the page links get their own row, and the current page is scrolled into view.
  - The section links stay on phones; before, only the ↑ was left.
  - A list fades only at an edge with more links behind it.
  - The blog filter's checkbox is no longer stretched.
- **Tests.** `src/components/edges.test.js`.

| ![](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/responsive/home-360-dark.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/responsive/home-360-light.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/responsive/settings-768-dark.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-15-c7170c04f74e/docs/case-studies/issue-15/screenshots/responsive/home-1920-dark.png?raw=true) |

## Better than konard/immortality

| | immortality | This site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Settings | about 50 axes | 251, each checked by a test to be applied |
| Presets | 12 built-in | 9 built-in with live miniatures, plus named saved looks (JSON export and import, synced between tabs) |
| Frames | one style per panel | each corner on its own: 7 shapes × 5 lines with preview tiles |
| Background | a set of backgrounds | five layers with strengths, up to 4 star layers with 12 shapes, beams, grid styles |
| Sound | effects per event | its 26 effects plus 5, up to 4 per interaction with levels and play modes, room echo, stereo |
| Phones | not measured | measured, a governor, optional parts loaded lazily |

## Checks

- `npm run test:ci`: 533 tests in 25 files pass.
- `npm run check` passes: ESLint, Prettier, the 1500-line limit and secretlint.
- `npm run build` passes.
- **Dependencies.** `npm audit` in CI failed on four new moderate advisories in `fast-uri`, which secretlint uses through `ajv`. `npm audit fix` updated the lockfile to `fast-uri` 3.1.9.
- **Cleanup.** The `.gitkeep` file from the initial commit is removed.

body:
Fixes #13

Each item of the issue is listed below with its solution and the test that checks it. The full analysis is in the case study [`docs/case-studies/issue-13/README.md`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/README.md). It covers the root cause of the rain bug, the decisions, a requirement → implementation → test table, the settings, the skins, the gallery counts and the stack.

## The matrix rain scaled up too much in Safari

![the reported screenshot](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/issue-reported.png?raw=true)

- **Root cause.**
  - The rain and the universe canvases took their size from CSS once at start, then listened only to the window `resize` event.
  - WebKit can run `<script type="module">` before the stylesheet is applied ([WebKit bug 261655](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=261655)). At that moment a canvas measures the default 300×150, so its bitmap is 300 px wide.
  - When the CSS arrives, the canvas grows to fill the window. The window itself does not change, so no `resize` event fires and the 300 px bitmap stays stretched (×4.27 on a 1280 px window).
  - It only shows up on some refreshes and menu clicks because whether the cached stylesheet loads in time differs from load to load.
- **How to reproduce.** `npm run build && npm run preview`, then `node experiments/rain-scale.mjs http://localhost:4173 late`. This attaches the stylesheet after the scripts run, as Safari does. Before the fix it printed "stretched ×4.27" on load, after a menu click and after a reload. After the fix it prints ×1.
- **Fix.** `src/visuals/size.js` adds `watchSize`: a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas itself, plus the window `resize` event to catch `devicePixelRatio` changes. The rain and the universe use it, and they do not redraw when the size has not changed.
- **Test.** `src/components/visuals.test.jsx` grows a canvas from 300×150 to the window size without a window event and checks that the bitmap follows.

| Before (late stylesheet, ×4.27) | After (×1) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/rain-stretched-before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/rain-fixed-after.png?raw=true) |

## Settings page

![settings page](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/settings-page.png?raw=true)

- **Where.** `/settings/`, linked from the footer of every page.
- **What.** 70 settings in 9 sections:
  - background animation;
  - universe (11);
  - grid (5);
  - rain of link networks (14);
  - skin;
  - glass (4);
  - liquid glass (16);
  - futuristic (17);
  - links theory notation.
- **Instant preview.** Every change applies at once: the page and its background are the preview. The universe, the grid and the rain read the settings while running. "Look at the background" hides the page for a moment.
- **localStorage.**
  - Only the changes from the defaults are saved, under `settings`.
  - Values are checked when loaded: ranges are clamped and choices and colours validated.
  - They are applied by a pre-paint script, so the page never flashes the defaults.
  - Other open tabs follow along.
- **Reset and share.** Reset one setting, a section or everything. Copy the changes as JSON and load them back.
- **Defaults.** They equal the site's previous values, so nothing changes for a visitor until they change something.
- **Tests.** `src/settings/settings.test.js` and `src/pages/settings.test.jsx`.

## Liquid glass skin

16 settings:

- blur, saturation, brightness, tint colour and level, radius;
- edge light and width, depth, shadow, sheen;
- floating panels, capsule buttons;
- SVG refraction, with strength and detail. Refraction needs `backdrop-filter: url()`, so it only works in Chromium; other browsers keep the blur.

The existing glass skin stays the default, and its opacity, blur, bar and radius are now settings too.

| Dark | Light |
| --- | --- |
| ![liquid dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/skin-liquid-dark.png?raw=true) | ![liquid light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/skin-liquid-light.png?raw=true) |

## Futuristic skin (after konard/immortality)

17 settings:

- **12 palettes:** mission, tron, ares, clu, athena, aphrodite, poseidon, soulextract, glitchy, amber, matrix and monochrome. Contrast is checked by `experiments/future-palettes.mjs`.
- **8 frames:** corners, chamfer, octagon, kranox, bracket, lines, underline and plain, with cut and corner sizes.
- **9 surfaces**, with opacity and blur.
- **The rest:** line width, accent bar, glow, display and body fonts, case, spacing, title style, hover effect and scanlines.

Tests are in `src/skins.test.jsx`.

| Dark | Light | Kranox frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![future dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/skin-future-dark.png?raw=true) | ![future light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/skin-future-light.png?raw=true) | ![kranox](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/skin-future-kranox.png?raw=true) |

## "Show only real references" in "Every configuration of 1–4 links"

- **What it does.** Leaves out every network that refers to 0, so every digit is one of 1…N. That gives N^(2N) networks instead of (N+1)^(2N):

  | Links | Default | Only real references |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1 | 4 | 1 |
  | 2 | 81 | 16 |
  | 3 | 4,096 | 729 |
  | 4 | 390,625 | 65,536 |

- **Defaults and combinations.** It is off by default and combines with "One per renaming". The rain has its own `rain.real` option, also off by default.
- **Implementation.** `codeAt`, `networkCount`, `classCount` and `representatives` take `{ real }`.
- **Tests.** `src/links/links.test.js` and `src/components/visuals.test.jsx`.

| Default, 2 links (81) | Only real references, 2 links (16) |
| --- | --- |
| ![default](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/gallery-default.png?raw=true) | ![real](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/gallery-real.png?raw=true) |

## The associative stack: every project, from the meta-theory up

![stack](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/stack-theory-first.png?raw=true)

- **Structure.** `src/data/stack.js` has 13 layers and 191 repositories, each with an EN/RU note. The stack starts from `link-foundation/meta-theory`. The layers are:
  1. theory & logic;
  2. notation & languages;
  3. storage engines;
  4. platform libraries;
  5. code translators;
  6. query, formats & viewers;
  7. benchmarks;
  8. Deep platform;
  9. developer tools;
  10. GitHub & GitLab automation;
  11. AI-driven development;
  12. AI on links;
  13. applications & community.
- **Navigation.** An index of the layers with their counts sits above the stack.
- **Coverage.** All 183 original repositories of linksplatform (76), link-foundation (79) and link-assistant (28) are in exactly one layer. A test fails if a new one is not placed, or if one is placed twice.
- **What is not shown** (the same rules as in issue #9):
  - forks;
  - private repositories;
  - the 86 deep-foundation mirrors;
  - 11 repositories that hold nothing but a README or a license.
- **New repository.** `link-foundation/lfs` was created after the last data collection. It is now collected (`experiments/collect-repository.cjs`, `collect-repository-health.cjs --only=…`) and placed among the storage engines.

## L → L² or R → R²

- **The choice.** `theory.notation` in the settings picks L → L² from draft 0.0.2 (the default) or R → R² from the latest draft, 0.0.3 of [link-foundation/meta-theory](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory).
- **"And so on."** The whole family of formulas switches together, for example Tₙ = Rⁿ, L = R × Tₙ and N²: R → R × R. The switch applies to the theory, the footer motto, the hero, the stack, the projects, the timeline and the positions.
- **What stays.** Free text is rewritten only where it contains the formula itself, so "Links" or "URL → URL²" stay unchanged.
- **Tests.** `src/links/notation.test.jsx`.

| L → L² (default) | R → R² |
| --- | --- |
| ![L](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/notation-l.png?raw=true) | ![R](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-13-b89681e2026e/docs/case-studies/issue-13/screenshots/notation-r.png?raw=true) |

## Checks

- `npm run test:ci`: 430 tests in 16 files pass.
- `npm run check` passes: ESLint, Prettier, the 1500-line limit and secretlint.
- `npm run build` passes.
- The `.gitkeep` file from the initial commit is removed.
title: Rain fixed in Safari; settings page with instant preview; liquid glass and futuristic skins; only real references; every project in the associative stack; R → R² notation

body:
Fixes #11

Each item of the issue is listed below with its solution and the test that checks it. The full analysis is in the case study [`docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md). It covers the sources, the decisions, a requirement → implementation → test table, the PDF pipeline and the ATS reading-order finding.

## Experience synced with hh.ru

- **New jobs.**
  - Evirma: Tech Lead, May 2026 – present.
  - Capico LLC: Senior Software Engineer, Nov 2025 – May 2026, Tbilisi.
  - Both have the achievements, stacks and roles from the issue.
- **Fixed jobs.** The dates, real titles, achievements and stacks now match the issue's table:
  - Kaiten: Development Team Lead until Nov 2025, with a team of 5 senior developers.
  - Deep.Foundation: from Sep 2022, with all the demo projects.
  - Abracar, ELAR, Termika, Pegas, AlpOnline and AsgardRo.
  - ArtBridge: Web Developer.
  - "Lead Developer" is no longer used for every job.
- **LinksPlatform** stays 2010 – present. Only its 2015 – 2020 employment counts towards the total, so the total is **18 years**, as on hh.ru. It is computed, not hard-coded.
- **Education and languages.**
  - The "Digital tools in the modern office" course (2020) is added.
  - Russian native, English C1.
- **Russian legal names** are used in Russian: ООО «Абракар», АО «ЭЛАР», ЗАО «Термика».
- **The data.**
  - Jobs moved to `src/data/experience.js`, with `{ en, ru }` texts and bullets tagged by topic.
  - Positions are in `src/data/positions.js`.
  - Private data from hh.ru (phone, birth date, salary, email) is left out, and a test guards against it.

## New positions

The old positions stay: ML/AI, DevOps, Lead, Developer and Research. The issue's nine new positions are added:

- Tech Lead / Team Lead
- CTO / Architect
- Backend
- Full-stack
- .NET / C#
- Rust
- AI Agents / LLM
- Trading systems
- Data Engineer

Each one has an EN/RU title and summary, plus its own jobs, skills, products and CV. All of them can be chosen on the experience page.

![experience page with the CV buttons](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/experience-cv-buttons-light.png?raw=true)

## CV per position, style and language

- **"Download CV"** on the home page and the experience page leads to `/cv/?role=…&style=…&lang=…`. That page has a preview, a position and a style picker, "Download PDF" and "Print / save as PDF".
- **4 styles:**
  - Classic: the reference structure.
  - Compact: one page.
  - Technical: stack, repository and package links.
  - Academic: research and publications.
- **ATS-friendly:** one column, one font, one accent color, real text, and no tables, images or SVG. Contacts are only GitHub, Telegram and the website.
- **15 positions × 4 styles × 2 languages = 120 PDFs.** `npm run build:cv` prints them with headless Chromium after `npm run build` in the Pages workflow. They are published at `/cv/pdf/konstantin-diachenko-<position>-<style>-<lang>.pdf`.
- **The build fails if:**
  - a CV for a position takes more than 2 pages;
  - a compact CV takes more than 1 page;
  - a PDF has no text layer;
  - any part of the CV is positioned.
- **Page counts:** the longest tailored CV takes 1.78 pages, and every compact one takes 1 page. The full record (no position) keeps every job and takes 3 pages.
- **Fitting 2 pages:** positions with more than 10 jobs, i.e. Developer, list the jobs that ended before 2015 in one "Earlier experience" line.
- **Finding: the ATS reading order.**
  - The first PDFs placed every job bullet after the last job in the extracted text. Chrome writes positioned elements (here, the custom `li::before` bullet) later in the PDF content stream.
  - Plain list markers fixed it, and the build now rejects positioned parts.

| Classic | Compact | Classic, Russian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![classic](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-classic-en.png?raw=true) | ![compact](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-compact-en.png?raw=true) | ![classic ru](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-classic-ru.png?raw=true) |

| Technical | Academic |
| --- | --- |
| ![technical](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-technical-en.png?raw=true) | ![academic](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-academic-en.png?raw=true) |

## Themes and languages

- **Light and dark themes** on every page and in the CV preview.
  - They follow `prefers-color-scheme` by default.
  - The top-bar switch cycles system → light → dark and is remembered.
  - The theme is applied before the first paint.
  - Print and the PDFs are always black on white.
- **English and Russian** for the whole site and the CV.
  - Detected from `?lang=`, then the remembered choice, then the browser.
  - The EN/RU switch updates the URL.

| CV page, dark | CV page, light |
| --- | --- |
| ![dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-page-dark.png?raw=true) | ![light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/cv-page-light.png?raw=true) |

| Home, Russian and light auto-detected | Experience in Russian, dark |
| --- | --- |
| ![home ru light](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/home-auto-light-ru.png?raw=true) | ![experience ru dark](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots/experience-cv-buttons-ru-dark.png?raw=true) |

Every page in both themes is in [`screenshots/theme-*.png`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/issue-11-e1dc259e3177/docs/case-studies/issue-11/screenshots).

## Tests

341 tests pass with `npm run test:ci`:

- `src/data/experience.test.js`:
  - every job is complete (role, dates, summary, tags), and a job missing one fails the check;
  - the hh.ru facts;
  - the legal names;
  - the 18 years;
  - the positions;
  - both languages for every text.
- `src/cv/cv.test.jsx`:
  - a render of every position × style × language (120 CVs) with no private data;
  - the earlier-jobs rule;
  - the compact, technical and academic styles;
  - the CV page.
- `src/cv/pdfChecks.test.js`: the page limits, page counts, text-layer and positioned-parts checks of `scripts/build-cv-pdf.mjs`.
- `src/i18n/prefs.test.jsx`: language and theme detection, the switches and the pre-paint theme script.
- `src/workflow.test.js`: the CV PDFs are printed into the build before the Pages artifact is uploaded.
- `npm run build:cv` printed and checked all 120 PDFs.
- `experiments/cv-pdf-text.py` (pypdf) extracted the text as an ATS would: 120 PDFs, 0 failures. It checks the contacts, the section headings, their order and the absence of private data.

### How to try it

```bash
npm ci
npm run test:ci
npm run build && npx playwright install chromium && npm run build:cv -- --verbose
npm run preview   # then open /cv/ and /experience/?role=rust
```
title: Experience synced with hh.ru; a CV per position in EN/RU with 4 PDF styles; light/dark themes and 9 new positions
